raw.description:
SYSTRA Canada is part of the SYSTRA group, an international consulting and engineering group, a world leader in the design of transport infrastructures. SYSTRA Canada is an engineering and consulting firm whose primary focus is to offer transportation solutions, whether for passengers or goods: feasibility studies of building a new railway line, increasing the capacity of the existing infrastructure, privatization of a railway.

Context

The Mechanical Designer will design structures, interior finishes, and various systems and components for rail vehicles, including locomotives, passenger cars, freight wagons, and maintenance equipment. They will produce designs using SolidWorks, SolidWorks PDM, and occasionally DraftSight.

Missions/Main Duties

  • Design and modify structures, equipment, and interior fittings for rail vehicles, including component layouts, supporting brackets, and fastening systems in compliance with standards and project requirements.
  • Create bolted, welded, and sheet metal assemblies using various materials (steel, stainless steel, aluminum), and develop sheet metal patterns/models.
  • Design plastic and composite components and select hardware items per engineering direction.
  • Prepare material lists and produce detailed drawings for modification, manufacturing, assembly, and installation.
  • Develop assembly manuals and installation instructions.
  • Conduct dimensional surveys on-site or in the workshop to support manufacturing and installation.

Profile/Skills

Education: College diploma (DEC) in mechanical design or Bachelor's degree in Engineering.

Years of experience: 5-10 years experience in metal fabrication and mechanical design, including significant experience with Inventor or Solidworks 3D modeling software (Relevant experience with other modeling software may be considered equivalent).

Technical skills:

  • Proficient in 3D CAD design and drafting, specifically with SolidWorks, including the creation of detailed drawings and flat patterns for rail vehicle components.
  • Strong understanding of materials (metals, plastics, composites) and mechanical assembly methods (bolted, welded, sheet metal).
  • Capable of layout optimization and integration of components according to standards and project requirements.
  • Skilled in preparing material lists, technical documentation, and installation instructions.
  • Experience in dimensional verification on-site or in the workshop.

Personal and soft skills:

  • Detail-oriented and organized, able to manage multiple tasks efficiently.
  • Effective problem-solver, adaptable to changing requirements.
  • Collaborative and communicates clearly within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Clear verbal and written communication skills, both in French and in English*

*Reasons for requiring bilingualism: You will have the opportunity to work with a varied clientele, including both French- and English-speaking companies. Bilingualism is therefore fundamental to building strong relationships with our customers, understanding their specific needs, communicating effectively in their preferred language and facilitating strategic meetings.

SYSTRA Canada is committed to having a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer that values applications from all and offers employment equity based on the merits and abilities of candidates and personnel.

We use AI-enabled tools in our recruitment platform (iCIMS) for tasks like resume parsing and candidate matching. These tools do not make hiring decisions; all applications are reviewed by a human recruiter, and final decisions are made by our hiring team.For questions about our hiring process or AI tools, please contact .

title: Clinical Talent Recruiter
description: Brightside Health delivers life-saving virtual mental healthcare to everyone who needs it.

raw.title: Clinical Talent Recruiter
raw.excerpt: Brightside Health delivers life-saving virtual mental healthcare to everyone who needs it.
raw.description:
Brightside Health delivers life-saving virtual mental healthcare to everyone who needs it. We are powered by proprietary AI, purpose-built technology, a world-class clinician network, and a care model that rivals the best of in-person treatment. When combined with precision psychiatry and leading-edge therapeutic techniques, we’re able to improve outcomes for those with mild-to-severe clinical depression, anxiety, and other mood disorders.

We take an action-oriented, purposeful approach with everything we do and seek out team members who value collaboration and thoughtful prioritization. As a result, our organization is looking for the brightest and most innovative talent in the industry. We can promise you that, as a member of the Brightside team, you’ll have the opportunity to collaborate alongside smart and driven people while growing your professional skills.

Our prescribing network is at the center of our next phase of growth, and we’re hiring a Clinical Talent Recruiter to help continue the mission. You’ll work alongside the Talent Team recruiting for Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNPs) and Psychiatrists, interviewing candidates daily, building a deep bench of qualified applicants, and prioritizing multi-state licensed talent who can expand our coverage and help us serve more patients.

This is a high-impact seat for someone who knows the mental healthcare recruiting market inside and out: how prescribers think about telehealth, what drives them, and what it takes to get a prescriber from first conversation through onboarding and seeing patients.

What you’ll be doing as Clinical Talent Recruiter:

  • Report directly to Brightside’s Sr. Director of Talent Operations, and work closely with the Network Operations team to coordinate recruitment strategy.
  • Drive full-cycle recruiting for PMHNPs, from sourcing through interviewing, offer acceptance, and onboarding, in support of Rx network growth targets.
  • Conduct video interviews daily, assessing clinical background, prescribing experience, and telehealth readiness.
  • Build and maintain a bench of qualified, interview-ready candidates so we can move quickly as state and capacity needs shift.
  • Prioritize and source multi-state licensed PMHNPs, partnering with Network Operations to target the states where we need coverage.
  • Actively source through LinkedIn, job boards, professional associations, NP communities, and referrals.
  • Partner with the Talent Team and leadership to define and refine screening criteria, including licensure, board certification, DEA registration, prescribing experience, and patient population experience.
  • Manage candidates in our ATS (Fountain), keeping detailed interview notes and moving candidates through the funnel with urgency.
  • Contribute to team-wide talent projects beyond day-to-day recruiting, such as new hiring initiatives, process improvements, and special sourcing pushes, as business priorities evolve.
  • Foster long-term relationships with past applicants and potential candidates.

Requirements:

  • 2+ years of clinical talent acquisition or healthcare recruiting experience in high-growth environments, with hands-on experience hiring mental health prescribers (PMHNP or nurse practitioner experience strongly preferred)
  • Working knowledge of the PMHNP landscape, including state scope-of-practice differences (full practice authority vs. collaborative or supervisory requirements), multi-state licensure, board certification, and controlled-substance prescribing considerations is all a plus.
  • Experience sourcing candidates in highly competitive environments
  • Hands-on experience with high-volume and full-cycle recruiting using various interview techniques and evaluation methods
  • Knowledge of Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) (Fountain is a plus)
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • A bias for action, strong prioritization skills, and comfort working in a fast-moving environment.

Benefits:

  • A competitive salary
  • Stock options so you have equity
  • Fully paid for comprehensive health care (medical, dental, vision)
  • Pet Insurance
  • Life Insurance & Short / Long Term Disability
  • 401k Plan
  • Unlimited PTO and sick leave
  • Parental Leave
  • Work remotely
  • Additional memberships and perks

Work Environment & Culture

At Brightside Health, you’ll join a fully remote, mission-driven team that values flexibility and impact. You’ll collaborate with professionals across engineering, product, and clinical teams, all dedicated to transforming mental healthcare. Our culture fosters continuous learning, empathy, and cross-functional collaboration.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to equal employment opportunities based on merit, competence, and performance. Research shows that underrepresented groups often apply only if they meet 100% of the listed criteria—we encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ job seekers to apply even if they don’t check every box.

Compensation & Hiring Commitment

Final offers are determined by multiple factors, including location, experience, and expertise. If you have questions about compensation bands, please ask your recruiter.

At Brightside, we recognize that building life-changing technology for mental health is both a responsibility and a privilege. We set high standards while ensuring every team member is valued, trusted, and empowered in an environment driven by inclusion and impact.

raw.description:
Job Summary and Responsibilities

As a Coding Auditor, you will be a central figure ensuring accurate and timely reimbursement by proactively resolving medical coding claim defects before billing. You will play a vital role in optimizing our revenue cycle and maintaining financial integrity.Every day, you will meticulously research and review coding-related claim denials, providing expert guidance on corrections to prevent future issues and recover lost revenue. You will also proactively address pre-billing resolution of coding defects, safeguarding against reimbursement impacts.To be successful in this role, you will combine a robust understanding of medical coding and reimbursement methodologies, exceptional analytical skills, and meticulous attention to detail. You will demonstrate a proactive problem-solving approach, driven by a commitment to maximizing financial accuracy and efficiency.

As a remote employee, we will provide you with the equipment needed to work from home, including a laptop, docking station, dual monitors, and accessories.

Job Requirements

Required

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum of one (1) year of coding experience or two (2) years experience in any capacity in a health care environment or medical office setting
  • Requires one of the following coding certifications from either the American Academy of Professional Coders (AAPC) or American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA): Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Coding Associate (CCA), Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), Certified Coding Specialist-Physician (CCS-P), Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT), or Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA)
  • Working knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, disease processes and demonstrated knowledge of medical terminology
  • Requires critical thinking and analytical skills, decisive judgment and the ability to work with minimal supervision
  • Applicants must be able to work under pressure to meet imposed deadlines and take appropriate actions

Preferred

  • Associate degree in related field
  • Healthcare revenue cycle experience preferred

Where You’ll Work

Virginia Mason Franciscan Health brings together two award winning health systems in Washington state - CHI Franciscan and Virginia Mason. As one integrated health system with the most patient access points in western Washington our team includes 18,000 staff and nearly 5,000 employed physicians and affiliated providers. At Virginia Mason Franciscan Health you will find the safest and highest quality of care provided by our expert, compassionate medical care team at 11 hospitals and nearly 300 sites throughout the greater Puget Sound region.

About Us

EnergyLink Sourcing LLC serves as the centralized supply chain arm of Quanta Services and its operating companies. Our centralized approach enables us to establish stronger partnerships across our supplier and client networks, improve material availability, and drive greater certainty of delivery for our customers. We are proud to support dynamic projects that power communities and drive progress.Our team is driven by integrity, responsiveness, and a commitment to delivering results. At EnergyLink, we believe in building long-term relationships with our clients, our partners, and our employees – grounded in trust, collaboration, and performance. We are committed to attracting and retaining top talent by offering competitive wages, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for professional growth.

About this Role

EnergyLink | A Quanta Services Company

Build the Strategy. Own the Category. Power the Future. ⚡

At EnergyLink, procurement is more than purchasing materials. It's about building strategic partnerships, driving innovation, and keeping some of the nation's most critical energy and infrastructure projects moving.

We're looking for two dynamic, results-driven procurement professionals to join our growing Supply Chain organization:

  • Category Manager II – MRO & Renewable Energy

  • Senior Category Manager (Level III) – MRO & Renewable Energy

Whether you're a skilled category strategist ready to expand your impact or a seasoned leader who knows how to turn supplier relationships into competitive advantages, we want to connect with you.

The Opportunity

You'll play a critical role in developing and executing sourcing strategies across Maintenance, Repair & Operations (MRO) and Renewable Energy Infrastructure, supporting large-scale solar, wind, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and other complex EPC projects.

Your focus will include MRO supplies, industrial equipment, tools, safety products, replacement parts, maintenance services, and other essential materials that support project execution and operational reliability.

You'll partner with operations, engineering, construction, finance, and suppliers to drive cost savings, improve material availability, strengthen supplier performance, and support EnergyLink's continued growth.

What You'll Do

Make an Impact

  • Own the Strategy: Develop and execute category sourcing strategies for MRO and renewable energy materials, equipment, and services.

  • Drive the Deal: Lead RFIs, RFPs, competitive bid events, contract negotiations, and supplier selection to deliver measurable value.

  • Build Powerful Partnerships: Develop relationships with strategic suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and key stakeholders.

  • Deliver Savings: Analyze spend, identify cost reduction opportunities, negotiate competitive pricing, and optimize total cost of ownership.

  • Keep Projects Moving: Partner with project and field teams to anticipate demand, mitigate supply disruptions, and ensure material availability.

  • Know the Market: Monitor commodity pricing, supplier capacity, industry trends, and emerging technologies impacting MRO and renewable energy.

  • Manage Supplier Performance: Establish KPIs, conduct supplier business reviews, and drive improvements in quality, cost, delivery, and service.

  • Think Ahead: Collaborate with planning teams on demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and long-term sourcing requirements.

  • Reduce Risk: Develop sourcing alternatives, evaluate supplier capabilities, and strengthen supply chain resilience.

  • Challenge the Status Quo: Identify process improvements, leverage ERP and sourcing technology, and turn data into actionable business decisions.

What You'll Bring

The Experience That Matters

Category Manager II – Level II

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, purchasing, or category management.

  • Experience sourcing MRO materials, industrial equipment, maintenance services, or renewable energy-related commodities.

  • Demonstrated success managing supplier relationships, negotiating contracts, and delivering measurable cost savings.

  • Strong understanding of supplier markets, pricing strategies, forecasting, and supply chain risk.

  • Experience supporting EPC, renewable energy, utilities, construction, manufacturing, or industrial operations.

  • Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems, procurement analytics, and Microsoft Excel.

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • APICS, CSCP, CPIM, CPSM, or comparable certification preferred.

  • Travel: Approximately 25%

Senior Category Manager – Level III

In addition to the core qualifications above, you'll bring:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, purchasing, or category management, with significant experience in MRO, industrial equipment, or infrastructure-related categories.

  • 5+ years of direct leadership experience, including developing and coaching sourcing professionals.

  • Proven ability to lead enterprise-level category strategies, complex supplier negotiations, and high-value sourcing initiatives.

  • Deep knowledge of MRO supply markets, industrial distribution, equipment sourcing, and supplier performance management.

  • Experience managing large spend portfolios, driving multimillion-dollar savings initiatives, and implementing long-term supplier agreements.

  • Demonstrated success influencing executive leadership and partnering across multiple business units.

  • Strong business acumen, analytical capabilities, and experience leading organizational change.

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field required; master's degree and professional supply chain certifications preferred.

  • Travel: Approximately 25–35%

  • Leadership Responsibilities: Leads and develops a team of sourcing professionals.

What Sets You Apart

You'll stand out if you have experience with:

  • Utility-scale solar, wind, BESS, or renewable energy EPC projects.

  • MRO category strategies across multiple locations or operating companies.

  • Industrial distribution, electrical components, tools, equipment, PPE, and maintenance-related services.

  • Strategic supplier agreements, inventory programs, and supplier consolidation.

  • Cost modeling, spend analytics, supplier scorecards, and total cost of ownership.

  • Building scalable procurement strategies in fast-paced, project-driven environments.

What You'll Get

At EnergyLink, we believe great people deserve great opportunities, meaningful work, and benefits that support life both inside and outside the workplace.

  • Competitive Compensation: Salary aligned with experience, qualifications, and role level.

  • Comprehensive Medical Coverage: Choice of a traditional PPO plan or two High-Deductible Health Plans through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas.

  • Health Savings Account: Company contributions of up to $500 for individual coverage or $1,000 for family coverage with an eligible HDHP.

  • Dental & Vision Coverage: Plans through MetLife and UnitedHealthcare Vision.

  • 401(k) Retirement Savings: Company matches 100% of the first 3% contributed and 50% of the next 3%, with immediate vesting of matching contributions.

  • Company-Paid Protection: Short- and long-term disability, along with company-provided life and AD&D insurance.

  • Paid Time Away: Paid time off, company-observed holidays, and additional eligible leave programs.

  • Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development, leadership exposure, and advancement within EnergyLink and the broader Quanta Services organization.

  • Meaningful Impact: The opportunity to influence sourcing decisions that support critical energy and infrastructure projects nationwide.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex (including gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, and/or gender identity), age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and/or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status.

We prohibit all types of discrimination and are committed to providing access and equal opportunity for individuals with disabilities. For additional information or if reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application, interview, or hiring processes or to perform the essential functions of a position, please contact us the Company’s Human Resources department.

Overview

Archimedes is seeking a Analyst, Proposals to join our team!

The Analyst, Proposals role is critical to the client acquisition and retention efforts of Archimedes. This position works cross-functionally at a variety of levels to maximize sales and retention through the timely creation and management of competitive responses to Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and other sales related documents for a variety of audiences. The Analyst ensures agreed upon strategies are incorporated into persuasive, compelling, and customer-focused proposals. This position ensures the timely completion of a project in accordance with defined project management processes and quality standards.

Is this you? Find out more below!

Responsibilities

How do I make an impact on my team?

  • Support Archimedes' client acquisition and retention efforts by drafting responses to Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and other sales-related documents for a variety of client audiences. Sales support activities can include project coordination (e.g., planning, scheduling, organizing, and coordination), follow-up correspondence, and reporting.
  • Utilize expert-level editorial, grammatical, and writing skills to ensure all written deliverables follow and demonstrate tactical, strategic, financial, and sales-capture decisions.
  • Proficiently understand and continuously develop knowledge of business units target markets and trends in those markets and how the products and services are/or may be utilized in the target markets.
  • Utilize strong project management skills to initiate, collect and deliver on analytical tasks in collaboration with cross-functional SMEs.
  • Demonstrate an attention to detail and strong time management skills by developing and adhering to stringent timelines.
  • Support proposal content management and department processes to keep materials current and competitive.
  • Contribute to the department goal of improved efficiency and effectiveness, including identifying and providing insights into streamlining departmental processes.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and ability to work independently and in a team/collaborative environment.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

What our team expects from you?

  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably in English, Journalism, or a Communications-related field, or equivalent proposal management experience, required.
  • 2 years of experience writing creative, concise, strategically correct, and persuasive proposals (writing samples and writing test) required.
  • 2 years of experience developing and implementing complex winning business strategies, while incorporating a consultative-sales approach required.
  • 2 years of experience delivering quality outputs in a fast-paced and dynamic team environment where tight time frames and strict deadlines are the norm required.
  • 2 years of experience strategic proposal content development and project management experience or similar related experience required.
  • Participate in, adhere to, and support compliance program objectives.
  • The ability to consistently interact cooperatively and respectfully with other employees.

What can you expect from Archimedes?

  • Top of the industry benefits for Health, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • 20 days paid time off
  • 4 weeks paid parental leave
  • 9 paid holidays
  • 401K company match of up to 5% - No vesting requirement
  • Adoption Assistance Program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Educational Assistance Plan and Professional Membership assistance
  • Referral Bonus Program – up to $750!

Job Summary and Responsibilities

As our Coding Auditor & Educator, you will utilize advanced ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and CPT-4 coding systems to support the facility and Coding Service Center, answer coding questions, and promote standardized, compliant coding practices. Every day you will onboard and train new staff, perform coding audits, develop and deploy coding education, monitor and communicate regulatory coding/billing changes, and participate in strategic planning. You will work closely with the Coding Service Center leadership team to perform internal audits and deliver follow-up education across the system. To be successful in this role, you will possess expert-level coding proficiency, strong analytical skills for auditing, exceptional educational and communication abilities, and a proven capacity to standardize practices, ensure compliance, and strategically contribute to coding and regulatory billing. This role is open to remote candidates in approved states.

  • Provides written, detailed rationale and supporting evidence for recommendations on audit findings.
  • Delivers educational feedback to coding staff regarding audit findings in the form of emails, development of PowerPoint presentations, and education sessions with the coding staff.
  • Provides guidance to coding staff and management in identifying and resolving coding issues and answering coding questions.
  • Identifies documentation improvement opportunities that impact coding accuracy.
  • Responsible for performing internal audits and followup education, monitoring trends throughout the system.
  • Performs prebilling reviews of specific types of cases deemed difficult to code and prone to error, performs coding audits, and trains new coding staff, monitoring performance and providing feedback, as needed.

Along with CO, KS and NM, this position is open to remote/out of state candidates residing in only these states:

  • Alabama- Arizona- Arkansas- Colorado
  • Florida- Georgia- Idaho- Indiana
  • Iowa- Kansas - Kentucky- Louisiana
  • Missouri- Mississippi- Nebraska- New Mexico
  • North Carolina- Ohio- Oklahoma- South Carolina
  • South Dakota- Tennessee- Texas- Utah
  • Virginia- West Virginia- Wyoming

Job Requirements

Required

  • High School Diploma/GED
  • Current AHIMA credentials (i.e. RHIA, RHIT, CCS, CCSP RCC) or AAPC credential (COC, CIC, CPC, CPCH)
  • Five (5) years coding experience in an acute care setting coding all types of hospital visits/admits with a high degree of skill in inpatient and outpatient expertise
  • Two (2) years experience in internal auditing and/or coding education
  • Epic and 3M 360 experience
  • Must demonstrate competency of inpatient and outpatient coding and guidelines

Preferred

  • Associate's Degree or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree
  • Multihealthcare setting experience

Where You’ll Work

With more than 700 care sites across the U.S. from clinics and hospitals to home-based care and virtual care services CommonSpirit is accessible to nearly one out of every four U.S. residents. Our world needs compassion like never before. Our communities need caring and our families need protection. With our combined resources CommonSpirit is committed to building healthy communities advocating for those who are poor and vulnerable and innovating how and where healing can happen both inside our hospitals and out in the community.

raw.excerpt: About Widewail Widewail is a Burlington, Vermont-based technology company helping businesses better understand their customers, strengthen their online reputation, and make more informed business decisions.
raw.description:
About Widewail

Widewail is a Burlington, Vermont-based technology company helping businesses better understand their customers, strengthen their online reputation, and make more informed business decisions.

Our platform brings together customer feedback, operational data, and artificial intelligence to help businesses understand what's driving customer satisfaction, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver better customer experiences. From automating customer engagement and managing online reviews to competitive benchmarking and actionable customer intelligence, we're helping businesses turn customer feedback into a competitive advantage.

We're solving interesting technical challenges at the intersection of data engineering, artificial intelligence, automation, and cloud-native software development. We're continually evolving our platform, expanding our capabilities, and finding new ways to deliver meaningful value to our customers.

We're a collaborative, pragmatic team that values curiosity, ownership, thoughtful decision-making, and continuous improvement. We care about what we build, how we build it, and the impact it has on the businesses and people who rely on us.

Hiring in the following states: Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Maine, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Texas, Vermont.

Compensation and benefits
  • $100,000–$145,000 annually, depending on experience.
  • Widewail benefits include:
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with HSA, FSA, and dependent care account options
  • Company-funded Lifestyle Spending Account
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Combined time off and paid holidays
  • Remote-first working environment
Who we’re looking for

At Widewail, we're building technology that helps businesses better understand their customers, improve their reputation, and turn customer feedback into meaningful insights. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help us build and evolve the systems that make that possible.

This is a hands-on role with broad impact. You'll join a collaborative engineering team, working primarily with Java, Spring Boot, and Python to develop the backend services, APIs, and integrations that power our platform. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data Science, taking ownership of your work from understanding the problem and designing a solution through delivery and production support.

If you're a pragmatic engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, values collaboration, and takes pride in delivering well-designed, reliable software, this might be a good fit.

What you'll do
  • Design, build, and maintain backend applications and services using Java, Spring Boot, Kotlin, and Python.
  • Develop and maintain APIs, integrations, and data processing workflows that support our products and customer-facing capabilities.
  • Own the technical design and delivery of moderately complex projects, from initial requirements through production.
  • Build scalable, reliable applications using AWS, relational databases, and cloud-native technologies.
  • Integrate with third-party APIs and external data providers, ensuring reliable data exchange and processing.
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to translate business needs into practical technical solutions.
  • Make thoughtful architectural decisions, balancing simplicity, performance, security, and maintainability.
  • Build automated tests, monitoring, and observability into the systems you develop.
  • Investigate and resolve production issues, contributing to the reliability and performance of our platform.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and engineering planning, helping improve how we work together.
  • Mentor other engineers, share knowledge, and contribute to a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
Who you are
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, and maintaining production backend applications, implementing infrastructure as code, ideally in a SaaS or technology environment.
  • Strong proficiency in Java, Python, or a comparable backend programming language, with an interest in working across both Java and Python.
  • Experience with Spring Boot or similar backend application frameworks is preferred, but not required.
  • Comfortable working with AWS or comparable cloud-native technologies.
  • Experienced with relational databases, SQL, REST APIs, and asynchronous or event-driven systems.
  • Familiar with Git-based development, automated testing, CI/CD, and production monitoring.
  • Able to independently design, implement, and deliver moderately complex technical solutions.
  • Pragmatic in your approach: you understand when to invest in architecture and when a simpler solution is sufficient.
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability, with a track record of delivering high-quality work.
  • Comfortable working through ambiguity, asking thoughtful questions, and communicating progress and challenges clearly.
  • Collaborative and approachable, you value different perspectives, give and receive constructive feedback, and help others succeed.
  • Curious and self-directed, with an interest in learning new technologies and improving engineering practices.
  • Bonus: experience with data pipelines, third-party integrations, observability, or AI-assisted development tools.
Why this role matters

Our platform depends on reliable backend services, thoughtful integrations, and the ability to turn complex data into useful customer experiences. This role will help us evolve our core applications, deliver new product capabilities, and improve the reliability and scalability of the systems our customers depend on.

You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both our products and the engineering team, helping us build better software and deliver value to customers more consistently.

raw.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

Granicus​ is seeking an experienced and highly skilled Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) to join our SRE team. As a Senior SRE, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability, scalability, and performance of our services. You will lead efforts in building and maintaining a robust infrastructure, automating processes, and guiding the team to implement best practices in site reliability.

What Your Impact Will Look Like

  • ​​On-call Production Support: Provide production support on a shift according to the team on-call roster.
  • ​Work on the customer and internal engineering/implementation team raised tickets while not on-call for production support. For example, a client may request to correct some data on the database server which cannot be done through the web interface.
  • ​Work on SREs backlog items.
  • ​Monitor and Maintain Systems: Continuously monitor the health and performance of our services, systems, and infrastructure. Respond to alerts and incidents promptly to ensure high availability.
  • ​Automate Processes: Develop and maintain automation scripts and tools to streamline operations and reduce manual intervention.
  • ​Incident Management: Assist in troubleshooting and resolving incidents, performing root cause analysis, and implementing long-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
  • ​System Improvements: Participate in designing and implementing system improvements to enhance reliability, scalability, and performance.
  • ​Collaboration: Work closely with software engineers to understand application requirements, provide feedback on design and architecture, and support deployment and release processes.
  • ​Documentation: Create and maintain documentation for processes, procedures, and troubleshooting guides to ensure knowledge sharing within the team.
  • ​Capacity Planning: Assist in capacity planning activities to anticipate future needs and ensure that our infrastructure can handle growth.
  • ​Security: Implement and adhere to security best practices to protect our systems and data.​

You Will Love This Job If You Have

  • 5+ years in site reliability engineering, system administration, or a similar role, with a proven track record of managing large-scale, high-availability systems. Experience supporting AI/ML infrastructure, including model deployment, inference optimization, and integration with services like AWS Bedrock is highly desirable.
  • Expertise in Linux/Unix systems, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud).
  • Strong proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash, Ruby) and programming languages (Go, Java, C++).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML operations, including model lifecycle management, vector databases, and inference performance tuning.
  • Experience with the ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) for centralized logging, monitoring, and observability.
  • Experience with configuration management tools (Ansible, Chef, Puppet).
  • Exposure to AI/ML toolchains, including AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, and LLMOps frameworks.
  • Certifications: Relevant certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning – Specialty, Google Cloud Professional DevOps Engineer, or similar are a plus.

Pay Range

USD $80,000.00 - USD $100,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

The Team

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Culture

  • At Granicus, we are building a transparent, inclusive, and safe space for everyone who wants to bea part of our journey.
  • A few culture highlights include – Employee Resource Groups to encourage diverse voices
  • Coffee with Mark sessions – Our employees get to interact with our CEO on very important andsometimes difficult issues ranging from mental health to work-life balance and current affairs.
  • Microsoft Teams communities focused on wellness, art, furbabies, family, parenting, and more.
  • We bring in special guests from time to time to discuss issues that impact our employeepopulation

The Impact

  • We are proud to serve dynamic organizations around the globe that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place — quite literally. We have so many powerful success stories that illustrate how our solutions are impacting the world. See more of our impact here.

The Benefits

At Granicus, we offer a comprehensive and flexible benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance—starting from day one. Here’s what you can expect as a U.S.-based team member:

Flexibility & Balance

  • Flexible Time Off – Take the time you need to rest, recharge, and live your life.
  • Company-Wide Wellbeing Days – Paid days off to unplug and focus on your mental health.
  • Work From Home Reimbursement – Support a productive home office environment.
Health & Wellness
  • Multiple Health Plan Options – Including a 100% employer-paid plan.
  • Employer HSA Contributions – When enrolled in a High-Deductible Health Plan.
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program – Stay active, your way.
  • On-Demand Mental Health Support – Access to Headspace and other wellness tools.
Family & Future
  • Paid Parental Leave – For both birthing and non-birthing parents.
  • Traditional & Roth 401(k) – With a generous company match.
  • Life & AD&D Insurance – 100% employer-paid coverage for peace of mind.
Growth & Recognition
  • Online Learning Platforms – Fuel your professional development.
  • Competitive Salary & Bonuses – Your contributions are valued and rewarded.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Granicus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants and employees will be considered for employment and advancement without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, physical or mental disability, age, genetic information, sexual or affectional orientation, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, familial status, military or veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law.

raw.excerpt: About Widewail Widewail is a Burlington, Vermont-based technology company helping businesses better understand their customers, strengthen their online reputation, and make more informed business decisions.
raw.description:
About Widewail

Widewail is a Burlington, Vermont-based technology company helping businesses better understand their customers, strengthen their online reputation, and make more informed business decisions.

Our platform brings together customer feedback, operational data, and artificial intelligence to help businesses understand what's driving customer satisfaction, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver better customer experiences. From automating customer engagement and managing online reviews to competitive benchmarking and actionable customer intelligence, we're helping businesses turn customer feedback into a competitive advantage.

We're solving interesting technical challenges at the intersection of data engineering, artificial intelligence, automation, and cloud-native software development. We're continually evolving our platform, expanding our capabilities, and finding new ways to deliver meaningful value to our customers.

We're a collaborative, pragmatic team that values curiosity, ownership, thoughtful decision-making, and continuous improvement. We care about what we build, how we build it, and the impact it has on the businesses and people who rely on us.

Hiring in the following states: Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Maine, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Texas, Vermont.

Compensation and benefits
  • $100,000–$145,000 annually, depending on experience.
  • Widewail benefits include:
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with HSA, FSA, and dependent care account options
  • Company-funded Lifestyle Spending Account
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Combined time off and paid holidays
  • Remote-first working environment
Who we’re looking for

At Widewail, we're building technology that helps businesses better understand their customers, improve their reputation, and turn customer feedback into meaningful insights. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help us build and evolve the systems that make that possible.

This is a hands-on role with broad impact. You'll join a collaborative engineering team, working primarily with Java, Spring Boot, and Python to develop the backend services, APIs, and integrations that power our platform. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data Science, taking ownership of your work from understanding the problem and designing a solution through delivery and production support.

If you're a pragmatic engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, values collaboration, and takes pride in delivering well-designed, reliable software, this might be a good fit.

What you'll do
  • Design, build, and maintain backend applications and services using Java, Spring Boot, Kotlin, and Python.
  • Develop and maintain APIs, integrations, and data processing workflows that support our products and customer-facing capabilities.
  • Own the technical design and delivery of moderately complex projects, from initial requirements through production.
  • Build scalable, reliable applications using AWS, relational databases, and cloud-native technologies.
  • Integrate with third-party APIs and external data providers, ensuring reliable data exchange and processing.
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to translate business needs into practical technical solutions.
  • Make thoughtful architectural decisions, balancing simplicity, performance, security, and maintainability.
  • Build automated tests, monitoring, and observability into the systems you develop.
  • Investigate and resolve production issues, contributing to the reliability and performance of our platform.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and engineering planning, helping improve how we work together.
  • Mentor other engineers, share knowledge, and contribute to a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
Who you are
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, and maintaining production backend applications, implementing infrastructure as code, ideally in a SaaS or technology environment.
  • Strong proficiency in Java, Python, or a comparable backend programming language, with an interest in working across both Java and Python.
  • Experience with Spring Boot or similar backend application frameworks is preferred, but not required.
  • Comfortable working with AWS or comparable cloud-native technologies.
  • Experienced with relational databases, SQL, REST APIs, and asynchronous or event-driven systems.
  • Familiar with Git-based development, automated testing, CI/CD, and production monitoring.
  • Able to independently design, implement, and deliver moderately complex technical solutions.
  • Pragmatic in your approach: you understand when to invest in architecture and when a simpler solution is sufficient.
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability, with a track record of delivering high-quality work.
  • Comfortable working through ambiguity, asking thoughtful questions, and communicating progress and challenges clearly.
  • Collaborative and approachable, you value different perspectives, give and receive constructive feedback, and help others succeed.
  • Curious and self-directed, with an interest in learning new technologies and improving engineering practices.
  • Bonus: experience with data pipelines, third-party integrations, observability, or AI-assisted development tools.
Why this role matters

Our platform depends on reliable backend services, thoughtful integrations, and the ability to turn complex data into useful customer experiences. This role will help us evolve our core applications, deliver new product capabilities, and improve the reliability and scalability of the systems our customers depend on.

You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both our products and the engineering team, helping us build better software and deliver value to customers more consistently.

raw.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

Granicus​ is seeking an experienced and highly skilled Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) to join our SRE team. As a Senior SRE, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability, scalability, and performance of our services. You will lead efforts in building and maintaining a robust infrastructure, automating processes, and guiding the team to implement best practices in site reliability.

What Your Impact Will Look Like

  • ​​On-call Production Support: Provide production support on a shift according to the team on-call roster.
  • ​Work on the customer and internal engineering/implementation team raised tickets while not on-call for production support. For example, a client may request to correct some data on the database server which cannot be done through the web interface.
  • ​Work on SREs backlog items.
  • ​Monitor and Maintain Systems: Continuously monitor the health and performance of our services, systems, and infrastructure. Respond to alerts and incidents promptly to ensure high availability.
  • ​Automate Processes: Develop and maintain automation scripts and tools to streamline operations and reduce manual intervention.
  • ​Incident Management: Assist in troubleshooting and resolving incidents, performing root cause analysis, and implementing long-term fixes to prevent recurrence.
  • ​System Improvements: Participate in designing and implementing system improvements to enhance reliability, scalability, and performance.
  • ​Collaboration: Work closely with software engineers to understand application requirements, provide feedback on design and architecture, and support deployment and release processes.
  • ​Documentation: Create and maintain documentation for processes, procedures, and troubleshooting guides to ensure knowledge sharing within the team.
  • ​Capacity Planning: Assist in capacity planning activities to anticipate future needs and ensure that our infrastructure can handle growth.
  • ​Security: Implement and adhere to security best practices to protect our systems and data.​

You Will Love This Job If You Have

  • 5+ years in site reliability engineering, system administration, or a similar role, with a proven track record of managing large-scale, high-availability systems. Experience supporting AI/ML infrastructure, including model deployment, inference optimization, and integration with services like AWS Bedrock is highly desirable.
  • Expertise in Linux/Unix systems, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud).
  • Strong proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash, Ruby) and programming languages (Go, Java, C++).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML operations, including model lifecycle management, vector databases, and inference performance tuning.
  • Experience with the ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) for centralized logging, monitoring, and observability.
  • Experience with configuration management tools (Ansible, Chef, Puppet).
  • Exposure to AI/ML toolchains, including AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, and LLMOps frameworks.
  • Certifications: Relevant certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, AWS Certified Machine Learning – Specialty, Google Cloud Professional DevOps Engineer, or similar are a plus.

Pay Range

USD $80,000.00 - USD $100,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

The Team

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Culture

  • At Granicus, we are building a transparent, inclusive, and safe space for everyone who wants to bea part of our journey.
  • A few culture highlights include – Employee Resource Groups to encourage diverse voices
  • Coffee with Mark sessions – Our employees get to interact with our CEO on very important andsometimes difficult issues ranging from mental health to work-life balance and current affairs.
  • Microsoft Teams communities focused on wellness, art, furbabies, family, parenting, and more.
  • We bring in special guests from time to time to discuss issues that impact our employeepopulation

The Impact

  • We are proud to serve dynamic organizations around the globe that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place — quite literally. We have so many powerful success stories that illustrate how our solutions are impacting the world. See more of our impact here.

The Benefits

At Granicus, we offer a comprehensive and flexible benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance—starting from day one. Here’s what you can expect as a U.S.-based team member:

Flexibility & Balance

  • Flexible Time Off – Take the time you need to rest, recharge, and live your life.
  • Company-Wide Wellbeing Days – Paid days off to unplug and focus on your mental health.
  • Work From Home Reimbursement – Support a productive home office environment.
Health & Wellness
  • Multiple Health Plan Options – Including a 100% employer-paid plan.
  • Employer HSA Contributions – When enrolled in a High-Deductible Health Plan.
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program – Stay active, your way.
  • On-Demand Mental Health Support – Access to Headspace and other wellness tools.
Family & Future
  • Paid Parental Leave – For both birthing and non-birthing parents.
  • Traditional & Roth 401(k) – With a generous company match.
  • Life & AD&D Insurance – 100% employer-paid coverage for peace of mind.
Growth & Recognition
  • Online Learning Platforms – Fuel your professional development.
  • Competitive Salary & Bonuses – Your contributions are valued and rewarded.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Granicus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants and employees will be considered for employment and advancement without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, physical or mental disability, age, genetic information, sexual or affectional orientation, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, familial status, military or veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law.

About the Role

Boogie Team is building a general Web Developer pool for current and future opportunities supporting U.S.-based businesses.

You will build, improve, and maintain websites and landing pages that are responsive, easy to use, and designed to support the client’s business goals. We will assess your actual platforms, technical skills, portfolio, and experience to match you with relevant client work.

Remote work aligned with U.S. Pacific Time (Los Angeles, PST/PDT), including daylight saving changes. Applications are welcome internationally. Exact shifts, working days, weekly hours, compensation, and engagement terms will be confirmed for each assignment.

This is a general recruiting pool; applying does not guarantee an immediate opening or placement. Full-time, part-time, and project-based opportunities may vary by client.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build, update, and maintain responsive websites, CMS pages, and landing pages using the platforms appropriate to the assignment.
  • Improve page layouts, navigation, calls to action, and lead forms to support usability and conversion goals.
  • Optimize mobile responsiveness, page speed, accessibility, and technical SEO fundamentals.
  • Connect forms, analytics, tracking, CRM platforms, and other approved integrations where required.
  • Troubleshoot website issues, broken links, plugins, scripts, and integration problems.
  • Test changes across relevant devices and browsers, and document updates and handover instructions.
  • Collaborate with marketing, design, and client teams while maintaining accurate content and consistent branding.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated hands-on experience developing and maintaining professional websites.
  • Practical knowledge of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and responsive web development.
  • Experience with at least one relevant CMS or website platform, such as WordPress, Webflow, or an equivalent platform. Clearly state which platforms you have used.
  • Understanding of website performance, technical SEO, usability, and testing fundamentals.
  • Ability to troubleshoot issues independently, follow requirements, and communicate progress clearly.
  • Professional written and spoken English, organization, and attention to detail.
  • A reliable remote-work setup and availability for the agreed Pacific Time schedule.
  • Include links to relevant websites or work samples in your CV, and explain your contribution and the tools used.
  • Submit your CV and a 60–90 second audio or video introduction using your own voice. Explain your relevant experience, the tools you use, and your Pacific Time availability. Audio-only is welcome.

raw.description:
About the position:

The Enterprise Solution Architect is a senior, client-facing architecture leader responsible for designing and governing complex Microsoft-based business solutions across multiple applications, projects, and workstreams. This is a full-time billable role that combines hands-on client delivery, architecture oversight, integration strategy, technical risk management, and strategic consulting. The architect translates business goals into scalable solution blueprints, guides delivery teams through implementation, and validates that the completed solution aligns with the approved design, enterprise standards, and expected client outcomes.

Your day might look like:

Solution Design and Architecture

  • Spearhead the design, development, and implementation of Microsoft-based enterprise solutions and integrations across multiple applications and projects.
  • Translate business capabilities, operating requirements, and client priorities into end-to-end solution architectures, roadmaps, and actionable design decisions.
  • Develop high-level architecture diagrams and models covering applications, data, integrations, security, and infrastructure.
  • Produce and govern solution blueprints and design deliverables that satisfy functional, technical, scalability, performance, reliability, and supportability requirements.
  • Define fit-for-purpose architecture patterns using Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure, ISV solutions, APIs, and custom development.

Architecture Governance and Quality Assurance

  • Define, maintain, and apply enterprise architecture standards, frameworks, principles, and reusable patterns.
  • Conduct architecture and design reviews for active projects to confirm adherence to agreed standards and Microsoft best practices.
  • Provide architectural guidance for large-scale implementations, programs, phased rollouts, and modernization initiatives.
  • Validate end-to-end readiness by confirming the configured and developed solution aligns with the approved architecture and original design intent.
  • Identify architectural deviations, technical debt, and quality risks early; establish corrective actions with delivery leadership.

Integration and Technical Leadership

  • Lead technical strategy for complex integrations involving Microsoft Dynamics 365 CE and ERP applications, Power Platform, Azure services, ISVs, external platforms, and custom solutions.
  • Recommend appropriate platforms, tools, and integration patterns based on client requirements, organizational standards, volume, latency, security, maintainability, and total cost of ownership.
  • Define best practices for API-first design, system integration, data movement, scalability, resilience, monitoring, and reliability.
  • Collaborate with solution architects, functional consultants, developers, data teams, and infrastructure specialists to resolve complex technical challenges.
  • Evaluate reusable components and architecture accelerators that can become internal intellectual property.

Client Delivery and Billable Engagement Leadership

  • Serve as a billable architecture resource across assigned client engagements, owning architecture deliverables and participating directly in discovery, design, implementation, testing, deployment, and stabilization activities.
  • Maintain billable utilization in alignment with company targets while balancing project commitments, architecture governance, and approved internal responsibilities.
  • Own assigned work plans, estimates, deliverables, dependencies, risks, and client commitments; raise issues early and support recovery planning when needed.
  • Facilitate architecture workshops, design decision sessions, technical reviews, and executive-level solution discussions.
  • Partner with project and practice leadership to ensure architecture activities are appropriately scoped, scheduled, staffed, and reflected in the project plan.

Pre-Sales and Strategic Consulting

  • Participate in sales handoffs, discovery, estimation, solution shaping, and project initiation to confirm technical feasibility, delivery assumptions, and alignment between the proposed solution and client needs.
  • Assist with estimating architecture, integration, data, infrastructure, and custom development efforts; identify dependencies, constraints, exclusions, and delivery risks.
  • Contribute architecture content to statements of work, proposals, presentations, demonstrations, and executive briefings.
  • Provide strategic guidance on cloud migration, application modernization, microservices, API-first design, platform consolidation, and phased transformation roadmaps.
  • Ensure pre-sales commitments are clearly transferred into delivery and traceable to the approved solution design.

Stakeholder Collaboration and Influence

  • Act as a trusted advisor to client executives, business leaders, product owners, IT leadership, project teams, and internal practice leadership.
  • Communicate complex technical concepts, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations in clear business language for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Influence solution strategy and technical decisions across functional teams without relying solely on direct authority.
  • Build alignment among business, functional, development, integration, security, and infrastructure stakeholders.
  • Work with leadership to align architecture strategy with business goals, client outcomes, delivery standards, and practice priorities.

Risk, Security, and Compliance

  • Identify, assess, and mitigate architecture, integration, data, security, performance, reliability, and support risks.
  • Ensure proposed solutions satisfy applicable data privacy, security, regulatory, and compliance requirements.
  • Embed security, identity, access control, auditability, resiliency, disaster recovery, and operational support considerations into architecture decisions.
  • Document material risks, assumptions, constraints, and technical decisions, including recommended mitigations and accountable owners.

Performance, Cost, and Operational Optimization

  • Define and promote practices that improve solution performance, scalability, reliability, maintainability, and operational readiness.
  • Assess enterprise systems and integrations for efficiency, cost-effectiveness, licensing impact, and opportunities to reduce complexity or technical debt.
  • Partner with delivery and support teams to establish monitoring, support, and transition requirements before go-live.
  • Recommend pragmatic improvements that balance business value, implementation effort, risk, and long-term total cost of ownership.

Innovation, Mentorship, and Continuous Improvement

  • Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend adoption strategies based on practical client value and delivery readiness.
  • Identify opportunities to apply AI agents, copilots, automation, advanced analytics, and data platforms to improve client outcomes.
  • Maintain relevant Microsoft certifications and remain current on Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure, integration technologies, security practices, and architecture patterns.
  • Mentor architects, consultants, and developers on architecture principles, design patterns, documentation, and decision quality.
  • Promote knowledge sharing, reusable assets, lessons learned, and consistent architecture governance across the organization.

What you'll bring:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering, business technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience delivering enterprise business applications, cloud platforms, integrations, or digital transformation solutions, including 3+ years in a solution or enterprise architecture capacity.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and governing complex, multi-application solutions in client-facing consulting or professional services environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365 applications, Power Platform, Azure services, APIs, data integration, identity, security, and application lifecycle management.
  • Experience creating architecture diagrams, solution blueprints, technical roadmaps, integration designs, decision records, and implementation guidance.
  • Ability to evaluate competing solution approaches and clearly explain trade-offs involving scope, cost, timeline, risk, scalability, and supportability.
  • Proven ability to lead discovery and design workshops, communicate with executive stakeholders, and influence cross-functional teams.
  • Experience estimating technical work and supporting statements of work, proposals, sales-to-delivery handoffs, and project initiation.
  • Ability to manage multiple client commitments, work independently, and operate effectively in a utilization-driven billable role.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Microsoft certifications in one or more relevant areas, such as Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure Solutions Architect, Azure Integration Services, security, or data and analytics.
  • Experience with Dynamics 365 ERP and CE applications, including Business Central, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Sales, Customer Service, or Field Service.
  • Experience with Azure Integration Services, including Logic Apps, Functions, API Management, Service Bus, Event Grid, and related monitoring capabilities.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework, Well-Architected Framework, ALM/DevOps practices, and enterprise architecture methods such as TOGAF.
  • Experience leading architecture for cloud migrations, application modernization, enterprise integrations, data platforms, AI-enabled solutions, or multi-phase transformation programs.
  • Prior consulting experience in fixed-fee and time-and-materials engagements, including scope management and delivery

Who we are:

Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Velosio’s 400 employees serve over 4,000 clients.

Beyond our expertise, as a Velosio team member, you can leverage the Velosio award winning culture - a network of top-notch peers, day-to-day flexibility, career development resources and the largest incentive opportunities in the industry.

Consertus is looking for a Senior Tax Manager to run day-to-day operations of the global tax function. Reporting to the Tax Director, this role leads compliance delivery across federal, state, local, and international jurisdictions, supervises the tax team, manages the external advisors who support it, and is a hands-on partner on acquisitions from due diligence through post-closing integration.

Consertus is a highly acquisitive, project-driven professional services platform operating across the United States, Puerto Rico, Latin America, the Middle East, India, and the United Kingdom. The right candidate is a technical tax professional who can manage people and deadlines, work directly with external advisors, and keep the function moving while the entity count grows.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Tax compliance: Own the compliance calendar for federal, state, local, and international returns, estimated payments, and quarterly filings
  • Transfer pricing: Maintain intercompany agreements, policies, and documentation for transactions across global operations
  • Cash repatriation, withholding, and cross-border transactions: Support the analysis and execution of tax-efficient distributions, intercompany settlements, and withholding tax compliance
  • Sales, use, and indirect taxes: Oversee sales and use tax compliance in the United States, and equivalent indirect tax registrations and filings as new jurisdictions come online. Partner with stakeholders to confirm the correct tax treatment of services and transactions
  • Tax due diligence and post-acquisition implementation: Coordinate information requests and working sessions with external tax advisors during diligence, assess findings, quantify exposures, and summarize risks for deal leadership. After closing, carry out the structure and integration steps: entity clean-up, elections, filings, purchase price true-ups, and onboarding of the new entity into the compliance calendar and enterprise resource planning (ERP) system
  • Process, controls, and systems: Drive improvements in tax reporting, compliance, and planning workflows. Develop and maintain internal controls, policies, and procedures that scale with expansion

  • Working knowledge of United States federal, state, and international corporate tax compliance, including exposure to Latin America, Central America, the Middle East, India, and the United Kingdom
  • Solid understanding of transfer pricing, cash repatriation, and international tax structuring
  • Experience managing sales and use tax and other indirect tax compliance
  • Demonstrated success supporting tax due diligence and post-acquisition integration

Skills

  • Strong project management, communication, and analytical skills
  • Proven ability to build relationships and collaborate across functions, including with Legal and external advisors
  • High attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, acquisitive environment

What’s In It For You:

  • A wide range of voluntary benefits, including pet insurance, pre-paid legal, hospitalization, critical illness, and accident insurance
  • 401(k) with day-one eligibility, including a 100% company match on the first 3% of eligible compensation and a 50% match on contributions between 3% and 5%

Job Summary and Responsibilities

As our Team Lead, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI) you will provide essential day-to-day operational leadership and subject matter expertise for a team of dedicated CDI specialists. This pivotal role supports the CDI Market Manager in driving crucial documentation accuracy, quality outcomes, and regulatory compliance, while steadfastly promoting consistency with enterprise CDI standards across our healthcare system.

Every day you will serve as a vital clinical and coding resource, offering guidance and support to your team. You will assist with critical performance oversight, ensuring our CDI specialists meet high standards and contribute effectively to our revenue cycle optimization. Furthermore, you will actively foster collaboration across multidisciplinary stakeholders, enhancing communication and synergy in achieving accurate clinical documentation and improved patient outcomes. This position functions as a hands-on, working lead, actively participating in CDI tasks.

To be successful in this role, you will need a strong background in clinical documentation improvement, healthcare coding (e.g., ICD-10, CPT), and a deep understanding of clinical pathways and regulatory guidelines. We are seeking an experienced CDI professional with proven leadership potential, excellent communication skills, and the ability to mentor and guide a team towards achieving superior documentation integrity within a fast-paced healthcare environment.

  • CDI Team Leadership & Support: Provides daily operational support, guidance, and functional leadership to assigned CDI staff, including workflow, prioritization, and issue resolution.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: Acts as a CDI subject matter expert, assisting staff with complex cases, DRG validation, SOI, ROM, and identifying quality documentation opportunities.
  • Performance Monitoring & Quality: Supports the CDI Market Manager in monitoring team performance, productivity, and quality metrics, contributing to improvement initiatives.
  • Quality Assurance & Education: Reviews CDI work for accuracy, consistency, and compliance, and assists with onboarding, mentoring, and ongoing education for CDI specialists based on audit findings.
  • Stakeholder & Workflow Collaboration: Serves as a liaison between CDI staff and key stakeholders (coding, quality, physician leadership) to promote documentation integrity and assists in developing CDI workflows and policies.
  • Remote Work & Ethics: Promotes a professional, collaborative remote work environment, troubleshoots basic technology issues, and adheres to ethical standards set by ACDIS, AHIMA, and/or AAPC.

Job Requirements

Required Qualifications:

  • Associate’s degree in nursing, Health Information Management (HIM), or a related healthcare field
  • Minimum of 3 years of recent CDI experience in an acute care hospital or large multi-facility healthcare system
  • Demonstrated expertise in clinical documentation integrity, DRG methodology, SOI/ROM, and quality indicators
  • Strong knowledge of anatomy and physiology, disease processes, medical terminology, and clinical documentation standards

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in nursing, HIM, or a related healthcare field
  • Prior experience in a CDI lead, preceptor, auditor, or informal leadership role
  • Experience supporting CDI quality audits or performance improvement initiatives
  • Familiarity with middle revenue cycle operations and downstream coding or billing impacts
  • Experience working with electronic health record (EHR) systems (e.g., Epic, Cerner, Meditech)
  • Background working with complex patient populations (e.g., trauma, cardiovascular, neurosurgery, or academic medical centers)
  • Proven ability to work effectively in a fully remote environment
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear, constructive feedback
  • CDI- or coding-related certification to be maintained, such as CCDS, CDIP, CCS, RHIA, RHIT, CIC, or equivalent

Where You’ll Work

Inspired by faith. Driven by innovation. Powered by humankindness. CommonSpirit Health is building a healthier future for all through its integrated health services. As one of the nation’s largest nonprofit Catholic healthcare organizations, CommonSpirit Health delivers more than 20 million patient encounters annually through more than 2,300 clinics, care sites and 137 hospital-based locations, in addition to its home-based services and virtual care offerings. CommonSpirit has more than 157,000 employees, 45,000 nurses and 25,000 physicians and advanced practice providers across 24 states and contributes more than $4.2 billion annually in charity care, community benefits and unreimbursed government programs. Together with our patients, physicians, partners, and communities, we are creating a more just, equitable, and innovative healthcare delivery system.
