raw.description:
About CData Software, Inc.

CData is the AI gateway between AI and the systems that run the business. One control point connects agents and individuals to data across hundreds of enterprise systems, grounds every request in company context, governs it down to the record and routes it to the most efficient model. Built on CData's data layer, it delivers accurate answers, governed access and falling cost, whether the user is an agent, an application or a person. CData powers AI workloads for Anthropic, Databricks, Microsoft, Google, Palantir and more than 10,000 customers worldwide.

Headquartered in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, CData has over 500 team members, with offices in North America, Europe, and Asia. We take pride not just in what we build, but in how we build it: together, with curiosity, creativity, and a shared drive to push boundaries. Learn more at or contact .

Senior Technical Customer Success Manager

Job Summary

CData's flagship product, Connect AI, is the gateway between AI and the systems enterprises run on. It gives agents and models such as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini live, governed access to hundreds of data sources through MCP. The same CData connectivity already powers Google, Palantir, Salesforce, Microsoft, SAP, and ServiceNow.

Our Customer Success team is small and growing as we focus on helping our largest customers adopt and grow their usage of Connect AI and Sync. We are looking for a Sr. Technical Customer Success Manager who can dig into complex use cases, translate customer needs into actionable insights for internal teams, and help customers get new AI initiatives off the ground.

If you are curious about how customers roll out and adopt AI, enjoy solving complex business problems, and want to bring those learnings back to the business, this role could be an ideal fit. Good ideas get acted on here. Show us why something will work and you can run with it.

This role reports directly to our VP of Customer Experience.

Location(s):Research triangle, NC, or East coast (preferred)
Eligibility: Applicants must be US-based and legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or in the future.
Key Duties & Responsibilities:

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Account ownership. You know where each account stands: on track to renew, at risk, or likely to churn, and why. You proactively identify and address account risks, take ownership of resolution, and keep key stakeholders informed of progress and potential blockers.
  • Adoption & Value: You build Success Plans to ensure our customers realize value from the CData products they purchased. You understand their use cases, identify opportunities to drive adoption and expansion, and serve as a trusted advisor when they encounter challenges or have new business problems to solve. Usage, expansion, and renewals are how your success will be measured.
  • Onboarding. You project manage onboarding alongside our Customer Engineers, who handle the technical setup. You keep milestones on track, bring in the customer's key stakeholders, and proactively address anything that could delay progress. Your goal is to help new customer reach their first working use case on time.
  • Partnership with Sales: You work closely with Account Executives to ensure customers renew and expand their usage of the product. You know when to involve the AE, keep them informed of customer needs and potential risks. AEs own pricing and commercial negotiations, while you bring the account knowledge and customer relationships that help drive success.
  • Executive and Growth Partnership. You lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and build strong relationships with executive sponsors at our largest accounts. You connect customers’ use of CData products to the business outcomes that matter most to their leadership teams.
  • Voice of the Customer. You bring customer insights directly to Product and Engineering, helping shape the future of CData’s products. You translate customer feedback, use cases, and business challenges into actionable insights that influence priorities and improvements. You work with a product team that responds.
  • Technical and AI expertise. You know Connect AI and Sync and how they apply to a customers’ technical environments and business use cases. You translate between the customer, Support, Product, and Engineering to help resolve challenges and identify solutions. While you do not own support cases or technical implementations, you understand what is behind them. You keep learning as new features are added.
  • Mentorship & Knowledge Sharing. You serve as a resource to other CSMs on technical and account management questions. You share best practices, document learnings, and contribute to the growth and effectiveness of the Customer Success team.
Qualifications

Must Haves:

  • 5+ years as a Customer Success Manager in B2B SaaS, with demonstrated results in retention, adoption, and expansion numbers from accounts you owned.
  • Experience working with customers on technical data, integration, or related enterprise software products. You understand SQL, APIs, and data pipelines well enough to follow a customer’s technical setup and engage in meaningful discussions about their use cases.
  • Experience using AI tools like Claude to improve productivity and an understanding of, or strong interest in learning, how AI agents connect to enterprise data, including LLMs and MCP. You are curious about emerging AI technologies and how customers can apply them to solve real business problems.
  • Strong communication, relationship management, and problem-solving skills. You can engage confidently with technical stakeholders and executive leaders, influence without direct authority, and navigate ambiguity in a fast-moving environment.
  • Experience using Salesforce and customer success platforms to manage accounts, track customer health, and maintain clear, detailed account records.
Travel Required:~10%

US Only: The typical base pay range for this role across the US is$120,000-$150,000 per year. The actual range may vary depending on specific locations.

Benefits & Perks / What you’ll Get:
  • As part of our comprehensive benefits offerings, we provide Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with company-paid insurance premiums
  • HealthSavingAccountoffering with company contributionto help mitigate increasing health costs
  • FlexibleSavingsAccountand Dependent Care FSA
  • Generous20-dayPTO and11paid holidays
  • 401k with 100% company match up to 6% of contribution
  • A remote-friendly, high-trust culture that empowers collaboration, celebrates curiosity, and encourages innovation
  • Work closely with your manager to define professional development and learning opportunitiesthat match your career goals

This role offers hands-on experience with the research, planning, execution, and analysis that help advertising campaigns succeed.

You’ll learn how different media channels work together to support client business goals while collaborating with strategists and channel specialists on real client work. Curiosity about advertising, an interest in data, and a willingness to learn are essential to success. Prior experience with advertising platforms is not required.

We have a trusting and flexible work culture, but it comes with responsibility. You’ll need to be disciplined enough to get things done without someone looking over your shoulder, bring great ideas to the table, and be unafraid to ask questions.

What You'll Do

  • Participate in training across paid media channels, including search, social, social commerce, retail media, programmatic display and video, connected TV, audio, and traditional media such as broadcast and out-of-home
  • Learn how client goals, audience insights, creative, and measurement inform an integrated media plan
  • Research audiences, competitors, and advertising trends to support campaign recommendations
  • Assist with campaign preparation, including keyword research, audience research, ad copy, and creative organization
  • Support campaign setup and quality assurance alongside channel specialists
  • Help track campaign budgets, pacing, and performance
  • Analyze results to identify trends and potential opportunities for improvement
  • Assist with reports and presentations that communicate results, key learnings, and recommended next steps
  • Collaborate with media strategists and channel teams to understand how campaigns work together
  • Contribute ideas for new tests, messaging, and ways to reach client audiences

What You Bring

  • Current enrollment in, or recent graduation from, a four-year university program
  • Interest in advertising, marketing, consumer behavior, or digital media
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Interest in building analytical skills and working with data
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the initiative to seek solutions and ask thoughtful questions
  • Eagerness to learn, adaptability, and openness to feedback
  • Certifications in Google Ads, Google Analytics, Meta, Microsoft Advertising, or other advertising platforms are a plus
  • Familiarity with Excel or Google Sheets is a plus
  • Exposure to advertising platforms, reporting tools, or data visualization tools is a plus
  • Coursework or projects involving media planning, advertising, research, or analytics is a plus
  • Experience with advertising through a student organization, internship, personal project, or small business is a plus

Hours, Location, and Pay

This internship begins in May 2027. Applicants must be available for at least 12 weeks during the summer and should expect to work approximately 20 hours per week. This is a fully remote role, with optional opportunities for local interns to connect and collaborate in person at our Raleigh, North Carolina, or Phoenix, Arizona, offices. Interns are paid a competitive hourly rate based on experience.

Why Join Us
You'll work alongside talented people who are passionate about solving problems, helping clients grow, and delivering meaningful results. We're a collaborative, fast-moving team where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed, and great work is recognized.

We believe the best work happens when people are trusted to take ownership, supported in their growth, and empowered to bring their unique perspectives to the table. Whether you're just getting started or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact while continuing to learn and grow.

Your cover letter is more than a formality. It’s our first introduction to you, so make it count. Applications without a cover letter will not be reviewed.

If you’ve made it all the way down here, we could be a good fit. We value attention to detail, and following these instructions is your first chance to show it off. We look forward to getting to know you!

raw.excerpt: Overview LMI is seeking HCD Assessment Practitioners to support a prospective VA OSP operational improvement program, contingent upon contract award.
raw.description:
Overview

LMI is seeking HCD Assessment Practitioners to support a prospective VA OSP operational improvement program, contingent upon contract award. These remote positions apply human-centered discovery methods and a government-approved assessment rubric to understand grantee capacity, implementation maturity, and barriers to effective delivery.

Working under the HCD / Magnify™ Lead, practitioners will facilitate discovery sessions, analyze organizational evidence, conduct initial and recurring assessments, and document findings that inform capacity improvement pathways. Rubric and assessment-framework development will be coordinated with designated subcontractor specialists; this role focuses on consistent field application and feedback on the approved tools.

This full-time practitioner works with fellow assessment staff and designated specialists. Strong candidates pair empathetic, structured discovery with reliable qualitative analysis, traceability, and practical recommendations for program leadership.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct human-centered discovery through interviews, document review, workshops, journey maps, and workflow mapping with VA OSP-designated participants.
  • Apply government-approved assessment domains, evidence rules, maturity criteria, and rubrics consistently across assigned grantees.
  • Review program narratives, workforce information, processes, data-collection practices, outreach activities, and other relevant grantee evidence.
  • Document strengths, implementation gaps, operational constraints, data limitations, and recommended capacity-building priorities.
  • Facilitate structured consensus discussions and validate preliminary findings with authorized stakeholders.
  • Maintain assessment notes, evidence trails, decision points, and rationale sufficient for repeatable reviews and quality assurance.
  • Translate assessment outcomes into clear inputs for individual capacity improvement plans and portfolio-wide learning.
  • Support periodic reassessment and verification of whether recommended actions improved the targeted implementation conditions.
  • Coordinate with the Magnify lead and designated framework/rubric specialists on tool usability, evidence interpretation, and controlled updates.
  • Partner with business analysts, evaluation and public-health specialists, and data staff to integrate findings across workstreams.
  • Observe approved privacy, accessibility, secure-information-handling, and respectful stakeholder-engagement practices.
  • Prepare tailored interview guides, discussion protocols, document checklists, and evidence logs for assigned VA-approved assessment engagements.
  • Use disciplined note-taking and qualitative coding to identify recurring patterns while preserving differences among participant experiences and organizational contexts.
  • Document the evidence supporting each maturity observation, clearly identify missing or contradictory information, and flag items requiring specialist review.
  • Facilitate respectful, accessible virtual discovery sessions with staff and community partners; use trauma-informed communication appropriate for sensitive public-health topics.
  • Contribute concise assessment narratives, illustrative workflow maps, and practical improvement recommendations that can be reviewed and reassessed over time.
  • Report observed rubric ambiguities and user-experience issues to the Magnify lead and designated subcontractor framework specialists without unilaterally changing approved criteria.
  • Tailor approved discovery instruments to each assignment while preserving the common assessment domains, consistent evidence standards, and comparability requirements established by the lead.
  • Identify the specific operational interactions behind observed friction, including role handoffs, onboarding steps, reporting burden, referral workflows, and points where staff need additional guidance.
  • Produce structured synthesis artifacts such as affinity maps, stakeholder needs statements, annotated workflows, and concise evidence summaries that enable peer review and traceability.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in design research, human factors, social sciences, public administration, organizational development, or a related discipline; equivalent professional experience may be considered.
  • 5+ years of applied human-centered design, user research, qualitative assessment, service design, or process-improvement experience.
  • Experience facilitating stakeholder interviews and workshops, developing workflow maps, and synthesizing documentary or qualitative evidence.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply structured assessment rubrics consistently and support defensible, traceable findings.
  • Strong writing skills, attention to evidence quality, and the ability to communicate implementation gaps without reducing complex organizations to simplistic scores.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and collaborative qualitative research or process-mapping tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound professional judgment, and ability to work effectively with federal stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen and able to obtain and maintain a favorable Public Trust suitability determination; must meet applicable federal/VA background, security, privacy, training, and system-access requirements.
  • Working knowledge of qualitative research planning, semi-structured interviewing, stakeholder mapping, thematic coding, and synthesis of mixed documentary evidence.
  • Hands-on skill with journey mapping, service blueprints or workflow visualization, virtual facilitation, and structured evidence repositories.
  • Ability to distinguish direct observations from inference and apply rubric guidance consistently across varied organizations and programs.
  • Familiarity with accessible digital facilitation, privacy-conscious interview notes, and quality checks for documentation shared with federal stakeholders.
  • Practical ability to plan and document research sessions consistently, including stakeholder-specific guides, careful notes, synthesis tags, and defensible links between evidence and conclusions.
  • Experience adapting virtual facilitation for participants with different familiarity with digital tools and varied organizational capacity, while maintaining respectful and inclusive engagement.

Desired:

  • Experience performing capacity, maturity, readiness, or organizational assessments across diverse grantee or service-delivery settings.
  • Highly desirable: Prior stakeholder research or assessment delivery on VA OSP/VHA, Veteran-serving, or comparable VA programs.
  • Highly desirable: Hands-on grantee management support, including grant-recipient interviews, evidence collection, self-assessment facilitation, and assessment documentation.
  • Familiarity with HSI, Magnify™/HPA methods, implementation science, or continuous-improvement frameworks.
  • Experience facilitating remote groups and documenting Section 508-conscious assessment materials.
  • Certified Usability Analyst (CUA), an established UX research certificate, Lean Six Sigma Yellow/Green Belt, or comparable methodological training.
  • Experience using approved qualitative analysis and collaboration tools such as NVivo, Dovetail, Miro, Mural, or similar platforms.
  • Experience supporting evaluation readiness, implementation-maturity assessment, or public-health improvement while maintaining clear boundaries from clinical care.
  • Training in ethical applied research, qualitative coding, trauma-informed engagement, accessibility-aware facilitation, or participatory service design.
  • Exposure to evaluating whether process improvements changed employee or grantee experience, information flow, or the usability of operational tools.

Target Salary Range: $88,000 - $125,000

Product Cybersecurity Engineer – Medical Devices

The Health Solutions Business Unit at Analog Devices is seeking a Product Cybersecurity Engineer to lead cybersecurity activities across the medical device product lifecycle. This role focuses on ensuring the security, privacy, and regulatory compliance of connected medical devices and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) solutions. The candidate will collaborate with internal and external teams to drive cybersecurity risk management activities, secure product design, threat modeling, vulnerability management, and cybersecurity compliance throughout the product lifecycle, from concept and development through post-market support.

A significant portion of this role involves performing threat modeling and supporting cybersecurity risk management activities aligned with FDA cybersecurity guidance. The successful candidate will also contribute to cybersecurity documentation supporting FDA regulatory submissions, including 510(k) activities, while helping to establish and maintain post-market cybersecurity processes and secure development lifecycle (SDL) practices for regulated medical devices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform product security risk assessments and threat modeling for medical devices and SaMD platforms.
  • Lead cybersecurity risk management activities throughout the product lifecycle in alignment with FDA guidance and industry best practices.
  • Support cybersecurity documentation for FDA regulatory submissions, including cybersecurity risk management files, SBOM requirements, and other regulatory deliverables.
  • Conduct security architecture reviews and evaluate system designs against secure architecture principles, cybersecurity frameworks, and regulatory expectations.
  • Develop and maintain cybersecurity risk management documentation, vulnerability management processes, and incident response procedures.
  • Partner with internal and external teams to integrate secure-by-design principles into product development and lifecycle management activities.
  • Participate in secure development lifecycle (SDL/SSDLC) activities, including security requirements definition, design reviews, and cybersecurity verification activities.
  • Analyze results from vulnerability assessments, static analysis, dynamic analysis, penetration testing, and security scanning activities.
  • Support SBOM generation, third-party software assessments, and supply chain cybersecurity risk evaluations.
  • Investigate and support remediation of cybersecurity vulnerabilities affecting medical devices, software platforms, and connected product ecosystems.
  • Participate in vulnerability management, coordinated vulnerability disclosure, product security incident response, and post-market cybersecurity monitoring activities.
  • Support internal audits, external assessments, FDA inspections, and cybersecurity reviews related to medical device security and regulatory compliance.
  • Serve as a cybersecurity subject matter expert (SME) for cross-functional teams and product cybersecurity initiatives.

Requirements

  • Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Ph.D. preferred.
  • 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity, product security, software security, or related engineering roles.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity activities for medical devices, connected healthcare products, or Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).
  • Demonstrated experience supporting FDA-regulated medical devices, including 510(k) submissions.
  • Demonstrated experience performing threat modeling for complex systems using methodologies such as STRIDE, attack trees, misuse cases, or equivalent frameworks.
  • Experience defining security controls, cybersecurity requirements, and mitigation strategies based on identified threats and risks.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity standards and frameworks such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 14971, IEC 62304, AAMI TIR57, and OWASP guidance.
  • Experience with vulnerability management, security testing, penetration testing, and remediation processes.
  • Familiarity with Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), third-party software risk management, and supply chain cybersecurity concepts.
  • Experience integrating cybersecurity requirements into Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL/SSDLC) processes.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Additional Desired Skills and Qualifications

  • Experience with connected medical devices, SaMD, cloud-connected platforms, or AI/ML-enabled medical products.
  • Experience with post-market cybersecurity monitoring, vulnerability disclosure, and incident response processes.
  • Experience with connected medical devices, cloud-connected platforms, IoMT, or digital health solutions.
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, HCISPP, GICSP, Security+, or equivalent.

raw.description:
The Opportunity

Lesley University's Department of Liberal Arts seeks a highly qualified adjunct faculty member to teach: CHIST 3322 — Black in America: Then Spring 2027 Term I; This course is taught remotely and asynchronously.


Course Description

The African American experience spans over four hundred years. For centuries, people of African descent in the United States have worked to help the nation realize its ideals of freedom and democracy, particularly since these ideals have been tied to their own status as free citizens. This course examines the shifting meanings of "freedom" and "democracy" for African Americans from the establishment of European colonies and the transatlantic slave trade to the present day in the age of Black Lives Matter. Topics covered include: slavery; the Civil War and Reconstruction; Jim Crow politics; the Great Migration; diaspora, nationalism, and internationalism; the long black freedom struggle and movements for civil rights; radicalism, feminist organizing, and Black Power; ghettoization and the prison industrial complex; and contemporary black politics since 1970.


Qualities and Capabilities

A successful candidate will have:

  • PhD or terminal degree (required)
  • Successful teaching experience at the undergraduate level; Experience teaching adult or nontraditional learners
  • Demonstrated commitment to student-centered, inclusive, and equitable teaching practices
  • Ability to effectively support students from diverse backgrounds and learning needs
  • Experience using learning management systems and instructional technology to support teaching and learning
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Why Lesley

Located in the heart of Cambridge, Massachusetts, Lesley University is highly regarded for its graduate and undergraduate programs in the human arts of education, the arts, and applied social sciences. Lesley fosters a highly creative environment in which innovative ideas thrive, theory is integrated with practice and its 6,400 students and 90,000 alumni are empowered to improve and enrich communities.

Lesley is committed to the ongoing pursuit of strategic diversity initiatives that help to position diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental to institutional and academic excellence at Lesley. In doing so, Lesley strives for a campus culture and community that fosters a true sense of belonging for all, provides opportunity for everyone to participate equally and fully in the Lesley experience, and helps to develop each individual's capacity to confidently and competently engage within and across difference. Given an evolving national context and the rapid change in the demographic profile of our country, the University has made a significant commitment to addressing and enhancing its campus climate and diversity capabilities as an institution.

Expressing Interest

A letter of interest, CV/resume, and a statement addressing past and/or potential contributions to diversity, equity, and inclusion through teaching, professional activity, and/or service must be included for full consideration.

At Lesley University we strive for a supportive and equitable environment where people -- regardless of race, ethnicity, color, sex, physical ability, religion, national origin or ancestry, age, neurodiversity, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, veteran or military status, membership in uniformed services, and all other categories protected by applicable state and federal laws -- can participate equally and fully as their true selves in all aspects of university life. Accordingly, the University prohibits discrimination based on these protected categories in any education program or activity that it operates, including in admission and in employment. We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the fabric of our institution. Individuals may submit concerns or questions related to discrimination to the University's Director of Equal Opportunity. Please visit the Office of Equal Opportunity's webpage for the University's entire notice of nondiscrimination and for additional information.

Lesley University Adjunct Faculty positions are governed by a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). To view our compensation targets for this position, please visit this link.

We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making.

Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here’s how the Senior Analyst, Pricing Analytics role will make an impact:

Key responsibilities for this role include:

  • Analyze portfolio, market, and operational data to identify opportunities, assess product performance and profitability, and inform pricing and commercial strategy. Develop clear reporting and visualizations that turn complex data into timely, actionable insights for business leaders.
  • Perform job functions in accordance with all applicable Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), federal and state laws, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) guidelines, health authority regulations, and departmental processes.
    • Work with leadership to understand and develop actionable insights from existing internal and external datasets available throughout the company to support product strategy and business decisions.
    • Coordinate and build strong working relationships with various internal commercial and technical organizations.
    • Monitor product performance by conducting extensive numerical analysis including sales, margin, market share, volume and inventory levels.
    • Proactively evaluate the portfolio to identify opportunities of growth to enhance the business.
    • Contribute to the development and improvement of analytics, internal reporting, and market intelligence.
  • Collaborate with colleagues to combine market intelligence, internal data, and knowledge of Viatris’ U.S. product portfolio. Track performance against commercial goals and marketing initiatives and provide timely insights into product and franchise profitability.
  • Complete Ad Hoc analysis and reports.
  • Prepare, integrate and analyze large datasets using data management, query, spreadsheet and business intelligence tools. Identify trends, validate data, and communicate findings clearly.
  • Develop and improve dashboards, recurring reports, variance analyses, and automated reporting processes. Apply appropriate analytical methods, including regression analysis, to answer business questions and support decision-making.
  • Use approved AI-enabled tools, including generative AI assistants, where appropriate to support research, data analysis, documentation and reporting. Validate AI-generated outputs, apply sound business judgement, and protect confidential and sensitive information.

The minimum qualifications for this role are:

A Master's degree (or equivalent) and experience in a data management or analytics focused role preferred. However, a combination of experience and/or education will be taken into consideration.

Ability to learn the interdependent market variables surrounding the products offered by Viatris’ subsidiaries, and the market channels in which they operate. Ability to perform business analytics relevant to the Pharmaceutical industry.

Able to assess complex business issues that require collaboration with multiple areas of the business, as well as articulate these business issues to management in a professional manner. Highly analytical, intellectually curious, detail-oriented, and organized. Able to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced, results-oriented business environment. Strong communication and interpersonal skills required. Proficiency in speaking, comprehending, reading and writing English is required.
  • Position functions semi-autonomously.
  • Ability to read and interpret complex business and/or technical documents. Ability to write comprehensive reports and detailed business correspondence. Ability to work with groups of people such as other departments and communicate known concepts. Ability to present to a group of departments.
  • Ability to perform computations such as percentages, ratios, and rates.
  • Ability to solve problems with a variety of concrete variables through semi-standardized solutions that require some ingenuity and analysis. Ability to draw inferences and follow prescribed and detailed procedures to solve moderately complex problems.
  • Typically sitting at a desk or table. Intermittently sitting, standing, walking or stooping.

Exact compensation may vary based on items such as skills, experience and location. The salary range for this position is: $55,000 - $105,000.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application process and employment, as required by law. Please contact Human Resources to request assistance.

We are actively seeking a results-oriented Regional Sales Manager to drive new client acquisition and expand market share within a designated territory. This role is pivotal in identifying new opportunities, nurturing prospective clients, and managing the entire sales lifecycle from initial engagement and property assessment to proposal delivery and closing new business. The ideal candidate will be a proactive self-starter with a proven ability to build strong relationships, navigate complex sales processes, and represent Watchtower Security as an industry leader. This position requires significant travel, active participation in trade shows, and involvement with relevant industry associations.

This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. Watchtower Security LLC does not sponsor applicants for work visas.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Sales Generation & Management:
    • Proactively identify, source, and develop new leads through prospecting, networking, and strategic outreach initiatives.
    • Execute comprehensive sales strategies using various methods (in-person meetings, virtual presentations, demonstrations) to achieve and exceed sales targets consistently.
    • Conduct thorough property assessments, both virtually and on-site, to understand client needs and propose tailored surveillance solutions.
    • Develop and deliver compelling proposals and presentations to prospective clients, effectively articulating Watchtower Security's value proposition.
    • Manage the full sales cycle from initial contact and negotiation to contract close.
  • Territory & Relationship Management:
    • Travel extensively within the assigned region for client meetings and strategic relationship building.
    • Actively represent Watchtower Security at trade shows, Apartment Association events, and other key industry functions, including after-hours participation. This includes engaging with attendees, presenting solutions, generating qualified leads, and fostering strategic partnerships.
    • Foster and maintain strong relationships with key community stakeholders, including law enforcement, property managers, and apartment associations, to support community safety initiatives and drive brand awareness.
    • Serve as a primary point of contact for client inquiries, interpreting concerns and collaborating with internal departments to ensure timely and effective resolutions.
  • CRM & Reporting:
    • Accurately enter, track, and maintain all lead and client information within the CRM system (ConnectWise).
    • Provide consistent and meaningful client and prospect communication via email and other channels.
    • Submit weekly sales performance reports and forecasts to the sales leadership team.
  • Professional Development:
    • Engage in ongoing sales training, technical education, and continuous development of industry knowledge to remain a trusted advisor.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Experience & Education:
    • 3-5 years of proven business-to-business sales experience, preferably within the multifamily housing or security/technology industry.
    • Demonstrated track record of consistently meeting and exceeding sales targets.
    • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent applicable professional experience preferred.
  • Sales & Communication Expertise:
    • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex solutions clearly and persuasively.
    • Strong negotiation and closing skills, built on a foundation of trust, transparency, and ethical business practices.
    • Analytical skills with the ability to interpret market data and client needs to formulate strategic sales approaches.
  • Technical & Tools Proficiency:
    • Proficiency with CRM software (ConnectWise experience is a significant plus).
    • Competency in Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace.

Working Conditions & Expectations:

  • Ability to travel significantly within the assigned territory.
  • Flexibility for after-hours attendance at industry events and client functions.
  • Standard business hours, with additional time necessary as required to meet business objectives.

For this position, Watchtower Security will review your motor vehicle driving record. If you express interest in and are considered for this position, you’ll be asked to authorize our review of that record.

raw.description:
We are knowmad mood!

Somos una compañía líder en transformación digital, en constante evolución y a la vanguardia de la tecnología.

Formado por más de 3.000 personas creativas, digitales e innovadoras conectadas a un propósito y capaces de generar conexiones con personas de todo el mundo. Un equipo responsable, flexible y con alta capacidad de adaptación a las necesidades de nuestros clientes y del mercado, a la vez que proporciona valor, visión, creatividad, expertise, profesionalidad y pasión por la tecnología en cada proyecto.

Los valores que marcan nuestro rumbo y nos guían hacia la excelencia son la colaboración, la innovación, el compromiso, la diversión y la conﬁanza.

Únete a nuestro equipo como 💻AI ARCHITECT 💻 para un importante cliente del sector bancario.

¿Cuál será tu misión en el proyecto?

Diseñar y evolucionar la plataforma de IA corporativa como producto que habilite a los equipos a construir, desplegar y operar capacidades de IA y sistemas agénticos de forma autónoma, segura y trazable, sobre el ecosistema híbrido de la entidad. El ámbito cubre la capa de acceso y mediación a modelos, el gobierno de su uso y su coste, la integración de la IA en el ciclo de vida del desarrollo mediante entornos de ejecución agénticos (harness) y el diseño de los controles que hacen ese uso auditable y conforme al marco regulatorio. El rol abarca tanto el diseño como la construcción de la plataforma y acompaña el producto a lo largo de toda su vida.

Requisitos mínimos

• Experiencia en roles de arquitectura técnica, habitualmente a partir de 5 años en su dominio de especialización.

• Experiencia demostrada y profunda en al menos uno de los entornos del ecosistema corporativo: on-prem (Kubernetes on-prem, VMware) o cloud (Azure, AWS, GCP), con comprensión del modelo híbrido.

• Diseño e implantación de plataformas de IA de autoservicio: mediación de acceso a modelos (AI gateway), credenciales, enrutado, cuotas y control de coste.

• Arquitectura de sistemas agénticos: orquestación, gestión de contexto, integración de herramientas (MCP, function calling) y patrones RAG.

• Harness engineering: diseño del entorno de ejecución de los agentes (contexto, herramientas, aislamiento, permisos y verificación) para que su resultado sea repetible y revisable.

• Gobierno de modelos: ciclo de vida de modelos aprobados, criterios de selección, evaluación de calidad y trazabilidad del uso.

• Seguridad específica de IA: prompt injection, fuga de datos y aislamiento de la ejecución de agentes.

• Observabilidad y control de coste sobre el uso de modelos y agentes.

• Integración de la IA en el SSDLC: pipelines CI/CD, IaC y ejecución de agentes en Kubernetes.

¿Qué ofrecemos?

  • Horario flexible ⏰: horario flexible entrada 8.30h salida 18h con viernes intensivo de 8h a 15h y en verano (julio y agosto) intensivo de 8h a 15h

  • Vacaciones 🌴: 22 días de vacaciones + 2 días de libre disposición, además de los días 24 y 31 de diciembre libres.

  • Contrato indefinido 📄: Desde el primer día, con opción de 12 o 14 pagas.

  • Retribución flexible 💳: Tarjeta restaurante, cheque guardería, seguro médico, formación y otros beneficios con ventajas fiscales.

  • Club de ventajas 🎁: Descuentos en tecnología, ocio y formación.

  • Formación continua 📚: Acceso a Udemy Business, cursos de idiomas, certificaciones oficiales y formación técnica.

  • Plan de carrera 🚀: Acompañamiento para crecer, especializarte o asumir nuevos retos.

  • Bienestar integral 💚: Programas de nutrición, actividad física y equilibrio emocional.

  • Conciliación +VIDA 👨 👩 👧 👦: Asistencia personal y familiar 24/7.

  • Ambiente inclusivo 🌍: Entorno diverso y multicultural.

  • Eventos sociales 🎮: Actividades para conectar con el equipo.

¡Apúntate y te daremos más detalles! 🚀
